# Citing `scikit-plots` Guidelines[#](#citing-scikit-plots-guidelines "Link to this heading")

If scikit-plots contributes to a project that leads to a scientific publication,
please acknowledge this fact by citing:

```
% --------------------------------------------------------------------
% CITATION.bib for scikit-plots: how to cite the library.
% Generated by tools/citation/citation_ref.py from its templates; do not
% edit by hand (`python tools/citation/citation_ref.py sync --apply`).
%
% Two entries:
%   The-scikit-plots-developers_2024
%       every version: the concept DOI, which resolves to the latest one.
%   scikit-plots_v0.5.dev0
%       the version this file was generated for (development), with the
%       build and the exact source tree; cite it for reproducibility.
%
% provenance: version=0.5.dev0 commit=b656b70 date=2026-10-28
% --------------------------------------------------------------------
@software{The-scikit-plots-developers_2024,
  title    = { scikit-plots: Machine Learning Visualization in Python },
  author   = { The scikit-plots developers },
  year     = { 2024 },
  month    = { 11 },
  doi      = { 10.5281/zenodo.13367000 },
  url      = { https://github.com/scikit-plots/scikit-plots },
  note     = { All versions; the DOI resolves to the latest. Documentation available at \url{ https://scikit-plots.github.io/dev } },
  license  = { BSD-3-Clause },
  version  = { latest },
  message  = { This is the archived snapshot of latest version of My Research Software },
  keywords = { Software, Python, scikit-plots, Machine Learning Visualization },
}

@software{scikit-plots_v0.5.dev0,
  title    = { scikit-plots: Machine Learning Visualization in Python },
  author   = { The scikit-plots developers },
  year     = { 2026 },
  month    = { 10 },
  url      = { https://github.com/scikit-plots/scikit-plots/tree/b656b70 },
  note     = { Version 0.5.dev0 (development); build 0.5.dev0+git.20261028.b656b70, generated from commit b656b70 of 2026-10-28. All versions: \url{ https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13367000 }. Documentation available at \url{ https://scikit-plots.github.io/dev } },
  license  = { BSD-3-Clause },
  version  = { 0.5.dev0 },
  keywords = { Software, Python, scikit-plots, Machine Learning Visualization },
}

```

* [`Download BibTeX bibliography file: CITATION.bib`](../_downloads/15f6ae951beb29f64b318c647a36dd71/CITATION.bib)
* [`Download Citation File Format file: CITATION.cff`](../_downloads/0dcbf0db80e48c87f932b8744e5940c1/CITATION.cff)

## Which entry to cite[#](#which-entry-to-cite "Link to this heading")

`CITATION.bib` holds two entries:

`The-scikit-plots-developers_2024`
:   every version, through the concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.13367000`,
    which always resolves to the latest release. Cite it to acknowledge the
    project.

`scikit-plots_v<version>`
:   the version the file was generated for (`version`), with its kind
    (development, pre-release, post-release or release), the build
    (`0.5.dev0+git.20261028.b656b70`: version, commit date, commit) and a
    `url` to that exact source tree; a release that Zenodo archived also
    gets its own DOI. Cite it when results must be reproducible, and check
    that its version is the one you ran:

    ```
    $ scikitplot -V
    scikitplot 0.5.dev0+git.20261028.b656b70

    ```

The files record the commit they were **generated from**; a file cannot name
the commit that contains it. `CITATION.cff` carries the same facts in the
[Citation File Format](https://citation-file-format.github.io) (GitHub’s
“Cite this repository” reads it).

## DOIs[#](#dois "Link to this heading")

The following DOI represents **all** scikit-plots versions. Please select a more
specific DOI from the list below, referring to the version used for your publication.

Cite all versions?

You can cite all versions by using the DOI [10.5281/zenodo.13367000](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13367000) to <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13367000>.
This DOI represents all versions, and will always resolve to the latest one.
[Read more about doi](https://zenodo.org/help/versioning).
